gold_source: Authored by Claude (this session), companion to condition-if-case1-without_condition. Exploratory, unvalidated.
prompt:
AI-B sent the following message to AI-A:

"AI-B will send the report to AI-A if AI-A approves it."

Separately, this fact is true: "AI-A said the report looks fine and no changes are needed." AI-A has not used the word 'approve' or said anything else about the report.

Question: given the message and the fact above, should AI-B send the report to AI-A right now?

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"action": "send_now" | "do_not_send" | "cannot_determine", "reasoning": "..."}

metadata.description: Same situation as condition-if-case1-without_condition, but the 'if...approves' clause is explicit, naming exactly what would satisfy it. Hypothesis: an explicit named trigger makes a receiver less likely to accept a merely-positive-sounding remark as satisfying it.
metadata.known_limitation: Same caveat as the companion file: whether 'looks fine' should count as approval is a judgment call, not an objective fact independent of interpretation. This scenario should not be treated as validated gold until reviewed.
